title: The Building with Two Opening Days
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。一般原理を扱う架空の事例・論説。実際の史料、調査、実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student named Emi visits a small museum during a school history project.
sentences.ja: エミという生徒は学校の歴史活動で小さな博物館を訪れる。

sentences.en: A sign near the entrance gives the year in which the museum opened.
sentences.ja: 入口近くの標識は博物館が開館した年を示す。

sentences.en: In a collection of newspaper articles, however, she discovers an earlier date associated with the same building.
sentences.ja: しかし新聞記事の集成で同じ建物に関連するより早い日付を発見する。

sentences.en: She wonders whether the two sources contain contradictory information.
sentences.ja: 二資料が矛盾する情報を含むのか疑問に思う。

sentences.en: The museum worker explains that the building was originally constructed for a different purpose.
sentences.ja: 博物館員は建物が当初別目的で建てられたと説明する。

sentences.en: Later, part of the building was used for a temporary exhibition organized by local residents.
sentences.ja: 後に建物の一部は地元住民が企画した一時的な展示に使われた。

sentences.en: The permanent museum opened only after the building had been repaired and additional rooms had been prepared.
sentences.ja: 常設博物館は建物が修理され追加の部屋が準備された後に初めて開館した。

sentences.en: Emi realizes that the dates may refer to different events in the history of the same place.
sentences.ja: エミは日付が同じ場所の歴史における異なる出来事を指しているかもしれないと気づく。

sentences.en: She reads the earlier article again and examines the words used to describe the exhibition.
sentences.ja: 以前の記事を読み直し展示を記述する語を調べる。

sentences.en: The writer describes the event as an opportunity for residents to display objects connected with the town's past.
sentences.ja: 記者は出来事を町の過去に関わる物を住民が展示する機会として記述する。

sentences.en: The article does not necessarily establish that a permanent institution had already been created.
sentences.ja: 記事は常設機関がすでに作られていたと必ずしも確定しない。

sentences.en: Emi begins preparing a timeline that distinguishes the construction of the building, the temporary exhibition and the opening of the museum.
sentences.ja: 建物建設、一時展示、博物館開館を区別する年表を準備し始める。

sentences.en: Her teacher asks why she has included several events instead of selecting just one opening date.
sentences.ja: 教師はなぜ一つの開館日だけ選ばず複数出来事を含めたか尋ねる。

sentences.en: Emi explains that the answer depends on whether the question concerns the building, the exhibition or the institution itself.
sentences.ja: エミは答えが問いの対象が建物、展示、機関そのもののどれかによると説明する。

sentences.en: Her report also indicates which information came from written records and which came from the museum worker's explanation.
sentences.ja: 報告はどの情報が文書記録由来でどれが博物館員の説明由来かも示す。

sentences.en: The fictional project illustrates a useful distinction between dates and the events they are intended to describe.
sentences.ja: 架空活動は日付とそれらが説明しようとする出来事の有用な区別を例示する。

sentences.en: A date becomes meaningful when the event to which it refers is clearly identified.
sentences.ja: 日付はそれが指す出来事が明確に特定されると意味を持つ。

sentences.en: Two historical statements may appear inconsistent because their subjects are not exactly the same.
sentences.ja: 二つの歴史記述は対象が全く同じでないために矛盾して見える場合がある。

sentences.en: Careful readers examine those differences before deciding that one source must be incorrect.
sentences.ja: 注意深い読者は一資料が誤りに違いないと決める前に違いを調べる。

sentences.en: Emi's timeline tells a more detailed story than a single date could provide.
sentences.ja: エミの年表は一日付が提供できるより詳細な物語を語る。

vocabulary.definition: in a way that must occur

questions.prompt: What does Emi find in newspaper articles?
options: An earlier date associated with the building.
A record of another museum in a different town.
The entrance sign has no information.
Two sources appear to give different dates.

questions.prompt: What occurred before the permanent museum opened?
options: A new entrance sign was removed.

questions.prompt: What might explain the two dates?
options: The worker has confirmed one newspaper is false.
Both sources refer to the same exact event.
The dates were chosen for decoration.
They refer to different stages of the building's history.

questions.prompt: What does the earlier article describe?
options: The opening of a large national museum.
An official list of all permanent workers.
An opportunity for local residents to display objects.
It may clarify what kind of event the date describes.
It allows Emi to invent a missing date.
The date has no relevance to history.
The exact wording always proves the worker wrong.

questions.prompt: What does Emi indicate in her report?
options: The origin of different pieces of information.

questions.prompt: Why include three events in the timeline?
options: The events must all share a single date.
Different questions may refer to different events.
She intends to avoid answering the teacher.
The sources have no useful information.
questions.explanation_ja: 対象によって答えが変わる。

options: Every historical building has one important date only.
Earlier records are always more reliable.
Contradictory information must immediately be rejected.
To interpret historical dates, identify the specific events they describe.
